newsitem.title: USA: TWA sees winter cutbacks saving millions.
newsitem.headline: TWA sees winter cutbacks saving millions.

text.p: Trans World Airlines Inc expects to save "tens of millions" of dollars by trimming winter operations by about three percent, an airline spokesman said Tuesday.
TWA's pilots union said it expects the savings to total about $25 million in the first three months of 1997.
While TWA scales back service each winter, "we're doing a little more this year," said TWA spokesman Mark Abels.
The St. Louis-based airline has reduced its trans-Atlantic operations but added some "sun and ski" flights to vacation spots, Abels said.
As part of reduced international service, TWA will park eight Boeing 747 aircraft, which are usually used on long-haul flights.
The company declined comment on whether the winter service cuts will affect workers.
In addition to the winter cuts, TWA is evaluating its flying plan for 1997. The company is expected to present the plan at a regular board meeting Tuesday.
The pilots union said the plan could call for a major reorganization of TWA operations at New York's JFK International Airport and a reduction in peak summer flying hours.
TWA said it did not plan to leave JFK completely but might some of its international operations to other cities.
"The roll of Kennedy Airport in our future is one we're considering," said Abels. "While Kennedy is still arguably the most important international hub, it's not the only international gateway,"

TWA's efforts to cut costs follow disappointing third quarter results. The airline lost $14.3 million in the period, due in part to unexpected expenses from an overly aggressive summer growth plan and cancellations related to the crash of Flight 800 in July.
